propositions: Test uses wall-clock threading.Timer to delete a planted index.lock during a git commit operation, but the timer can fire while git holds its own real index.lock, causing git commit to fail with 'unable to write new index file'.
On slow runners (macOS py3.13 leg ~23m vs Linux ~12m), git commit duration extends past the 0.4s timer delay, creating a window where the timer deletes git's own lock mid-operation.
The force_reclaim=True parameter bypasses the age gate and causes the planted lock to be reclaimed on the first retry attempt, succeeding immediately rather than blocking the full retry window.
Test-only race condition; production backoff logic is correct and succeeds, so no store or backoff behavior change is needed.
Replace the wall-clock timer with gitutil._retry_probe, a deterministic probe that fires after each retry attempt, allowing test to release the planted lock only after confirming the first failure.
